title: Microcohort Signal-Led Rollout Protocol (wip)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a lightweight, signal-first protocol for canarying features and model changes using small, targeted user microcohorts. Goal is to detect regressions quickly, minimize blast radius, and give cross-functional teams (product, SRE, ML infra, support) a single checklist and decision flow to run progressive exposure.

Context / why microcohorts:
- Typical full-cohort canaries obscure edge failures (device/os-specific, prompt-shape differences, corporate networks).
- Microcohorts = deterministic, repeatable subsets of traffic (by hashed user id, client-version, region, or test-flag) that amplify signal for specific regression modes.
- This protocol is for incremental releases where we want tight observation windows and rapid rollback if needed.

Scope:
- Applies to API-level model or feature deploys served via Redwood Console rollouts (hosted + dedicated).
- Not for infra-only deployments (kernel/driver) — SRE-run procedure exists separately.
- Intended for releases with measurable signal metrics (latency, error, model-quality heuristics, cost delta).

Definitions / terms:
- microcohort: deterministic subset (e.g., user_id % 1000 in [1..10]) used to expose traffic.
- signal-led gate: metric-driven decision point (numeric thresholds + direction).
- ramp-stage: discrete exposure step (examples below).
- hold window: minimum time to assess signals at a stage.

Microcohort recipes (examples):
- device-edge cohort: user_id % 1000 in [1..5] AND client_version <= 2.3.4 (target old clients).
- latency-sensitive cohort: traffic from us-east-1 with median request size > 2k tokens.
- enterprise-admin cohort: account_id in (list of 5 enterprise test accounts) — used for security-sensitive features.
- random-sample mini: hashed_request_id % 10000 in [0..9] (~0.1% of traffic).
Notes: prefer deterministic hash ranges over opt-in flags for reproducibility across reruns.

Signal taxonomy (primary):
- Latency P95/P99 (endpoint): relative delta vs baseline (percent).
- Error rate: 5xx and application-defined failures (parse errors, hallucination detection hook).
- Model-quality regressions: eval-set regression score (prompt-suite pass rate), per-prompt scoring functions (e.g., rubric-based auto-check).
- Cost/unit: per-token time/cost delta for the new variant.
Secondary signals:
- Ux telemetries (click-through, fallback usage), session aborts, customer support tickets volume tagged to feature.

Suggested thresholds (starting point, tune per-product):
- Latency: P95 increase > 20% relative to baseline -> immediate hold/investigate. P95 > 200ms absolute for synchronous flows -> high severity.
- Error: > 0.5% absolute increase in 5xx or application error codes -> hold.
- Quality: automated prompt-suite pass rate drop > 2 percentage points (relative) -> hold (requires review by ML owner).
- Cost: unit cost increase > 30% without quality uplift -> ticket for cost review; may continue if product OK.

Rollout stages (signal-led):
1) Pilot microcohort — 0.05% (example: hashed range) — Hold window: 1 hour or 500 requests, whichever is larger.
2) Small microcohort — 0.5% — Hold window: 2 hours + run automated eval on captured requests.
3) Focused cohort expansion — 5% (by targeted segments e.g., region or client-version) — Hold window: 6 hours + manual review if any metric degraded.
4) Broad ramp — 25% — Hold window: 24 hours (monitor long-tail errors).
5) Full exposure — 100% (or remain at steady-state if rollout as feature flag).
Traffic split pattern: pilot -> small -> focused -> broad -> full. Never skip stages without explicit cross-functional sign-off (product + SRE + ML owner).

Instrumentation checklist (pre-rollout):
- Dashboard: P95/P99 latency + error rate for canary cohort and baseline cohort.
- Auto-eval: capture 1000 requests from each stage and run prompt-suite; results surfaced to Confluence/Jira.
- Tracing: distributed traces enabled and linked per request id.
- Sampling: increased log sampling for cohort requests (configurable, default 10x baseline).
- Canary tags: add metadata to requests: rollout_id, stage, cohort_id for easy filtering.
- Alerts: Create ephemeral alert rules scoped to rollout_id that auto-expire after 48h.

Decision gates and responsibilities:
- Gate definition: a gate is a set of metric thresholds that must pass to move to next stage. Gates are signal-led but allow human judgment.
- Owners: product: rollout hypothesis & user impact; ML owner: model-quality; SRE: latency/availability; infra: cost/running limits.
- Decision ceremony: asynchronous on dashboard + 30-min live sync if any gate is violated. Primary owner (listed in rollout ticket) holds authority to pause/rollback.

Escalation matrix (quick):
- Stage-level incident: notify on-call SRE + product owner via Slack and PagerDuty (if severity > Sev2).
- Major regression (quality/latency beyond defined thresholds): immediate rollback to previous stable variant, create incident ticket, convene incident bridge.
- Customer-impacting: CS lead and account owner notified within 15 minutes of detection.

Rollback criteria and policy:
- Automatic rollback triggers: error rate > defined threshold OR latency P99 > upper bound for > 10 minutes.
- Manual rollback: any model-quality regression flagged by ML owner after manual inspection.
- Rollback plan: revert routing in Redwood Console to previous model variant, invalidate any caching that could mask regressions, and mark rollout ticket with cause, rollback time, and preliminary notes.

Observability and runbook snippets (copy/paste):
- Query: canary_latency_p95{rollout_id=\"<id>\",cohort_id=\"micro-1\"} vs baseline_latency_p95{...}
- Alert rule draft: if (canary_error_rate - baseline_error_rate) > 0.005 for 10m -> notify #prod-rollouts, page SRE oncall.

Coordination checklist before starting:
- [ ] Confirm rollout ticket exists and has owners + timeframe (Jira PROD-3421).
- [ ] Verify instrumentation (dashboard links in ticket).
- [ ] Create ephemeral alerting rules.
- [ ] Register cohort recipe and deterministic hash boundaries.
- [ ] Communicate to CS/support + on-call SRE with expected windows and rollback steps.
- [ ] Validate smoke tests and runbook steps in staging.

Comms templates (short):
- Slack kickoff: \"Rolling out model vX to microcohort A (0.05%). Owners: Asha (product), Maya (ML), Ravi (SRE). Monitoring: dashboard link. Planned hold windows: pilot 1h. Will escalate on any gate violation.\"
- Slack hold/rollback: \"HOLD: rollout PROJ-3421 paused at stage 2 due to P95 increase of 28% on cohort. Rolling back to stable variant. Details: <link>. Owning oncall: Ravi.\"

Post-rollout: analysis and artifacts:
- Postmortem checklist: attach eval-run results, raw cohort traffic sample, timeline of metric deltas, decision log (who approved each stage), and any follow-up tickets.
- Signal retention: persist canary data for 90 days for cross-release comparisons.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need a standard format for automated eval pass/fail that is lightweight (Maya to propose by 2026-03-01).
- Decide on default hold windows per product vertical (console team to draft).
- Explore automating cohort selection in console UI (product/infra spike).

Appendix: quick examples
- Hash-based cohort code snippet (pseudocode):
  cohort = (hash(user_id) % 10000) < 50  // ~0.5%
- Typical ramp timeline for low-risk UI tweak: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% with 2h/6h/24h holds.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep microcohorts small early; quality regressions often appear in the first 5000 relevant requests.
- Capture user prompts (obfuscated) for ML inspect — key to diagnosing hallucination spikes.
- If rolling out across dedicated pools, ensure routing policy keeps cohort on same hardware class (avoid cross-pool noise).

Next steps (short):
- Maya: prototype auto-eval pass/fail metric (due 2026-03-01).
- Asha + Ravi: run tabletop with SRE and CS next Wed to rehearse rollback flow.
- Samir: add ephemeral alerting template to infra repo and link PR.

Related artifacts: Confluence page (linked), Jira ticket PROD-3421, PR #1289 (runtime change), slack thread #prod-rollouts.
